# `Browser.WebAuthn.Internals`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.WebAuthn.Internals — the low-level Web Authentication port
surface: the closed outbound/inbound ADTs and the raw `Ipe.Ffi.Js`
request/subscribe wiring the high-level `Ipe.Browser.WebAuthn` layer wraps.

Importing this submodule discloses the same `js-port:web-authn` axis as the
top-level module (the disclosure is keyed on the `Ipe.Browser.WebAuthn` path
prefix), so the raw port surface cannot be reached undisclosed.

Credential material never crosses this port as a readable structure. A
registration or an assertion returns an opaque, base64url-encoded envelope of
fields — never a plaintext key. The inbound decoder is total and fail-closed:
an unrecognised token, a `NotAllowedError`, or an absent API becomes a typed
inbound variant, never a silent-accept and never a throw.

## `JsCmd`

The ONE closed OUTBOUND port type — the two ceremonies of Web
Authentication.

  * `Create opts` — a registration ceremony: `navigator.credentials.create`
    with `opts` as the `publicKey` creation options. `opts` carries the
    relying party, the user, the base64url `challenge`, and the algorithm
    preferences. A success returns an attestation envelope inbound; a host
    refusal or an absent API traps to a typed inbound variant.
  * `Get opts` — an authentication ceremony: `navigator.credentials.get`
    with `opts` as the `publicKey` request options. `opts` carries the
    base64url `challenge`, the relying-party id, and the allowed credential
    ids. A success returns an assertion envelope inbound; a host refusal or
    an absent API traps to a typed inbound variant.

Every buffer-shaped field (`challenge`, credential `id`) crosses as a
base64url `String`, never as raw bytes: the JS sink decodes it to an
`ArrayBuffer` at the boundary and re-encodes every returned buffer to
base64url, so no raw key material is ever representable in the port frame.

## `JsMsg`

The NARROW closed INBOUND port type — deliberately NOT the app's internal
`Msg`. Every variant the ceremony can push is enumerated, so the fold in the
high-level layer is EXHAUSTIVE and a refusal, an absent API, or a malformed
ceremony can never be silently mis-mapped: each becomes a typed value.

  * `Registered { id, rawId, clientDataJson, attestationObject }` — a
    registration ceremony completed. Every field is a base64url `String`
    envelope of an opaque buffer; the module NEVER exposes decoded key bytes.
  * `Asserted { id, rawId, clientDataJson, authenticatorData, signature, userHandle }`
    — an authentication ceremony completed. Every field is a base64url
    `String` envelope; `userHandle` is `""` when the authenticator returned
    none. The `signature` is opaque — the module carries it, never inspects it.
  * `Denied` — the host refused the ceremony (`NotAllowedError`, a user
    cancellation, or a security refusal). Terminal, fail-closed.
  * `Unavailable` — the Web Authentication API is absent in this context (no
    `navigator.credentials` or no `PublicKeyCredential`). Terminal.

## `request`

```ipe
request : JsCmd -> Cmd.Cmd msg
```

`request cmd` — hand a closed outbound `JsCmd` to the raw port transport.
The served first-party JS sink runs the ceremony; its result arrives inbound
as a `JsMsg` frame on the `subscribe` path.

## `requestOne`

```ipe
requestOne : JsCmd -> Task Error JsMsg
```

`requestOne cmd` — correlated one-shot `JsCmd` → `Task Error JsMsg`. Routes
through `Js.request` with the `inbound` decoder so the correlated reply is
decoded fail-closed by the same gate the `subscribe` path uses. A ceremony is
one-shot by nature, so this is the primary path.

## `subscribe`

```ipe
subscribe : (JsMsg -> msg) -> Sub.Sub msg
```

`subscribe toMsg` — the inbound subscription over the fail-closed seal
decoder. `inbound` IS the security gate; a malformed / mismatched frame is
dropped whole. A decoded `JsMsg` is handed to `toMsg`.

## `inbound`

```ipe
inbound : Decode.Decoder JsMsg
```

The total, fail-closed decoder for a `JsMsg` frame of this capability.

It first requires the frame's `tag` to be `portTag`, so a frame of another
capability, or an untagged one, fails closed; the rest decodes as `inboundBody`.
